page: Amazon Web Services r7gd.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by custom 64-core AWS Graviton processors utilizing the 64-bit ARMv8 architecture (Neoverse-V1) running at 2.6 GHz. It features 64 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, eliminating hyperthreading overhead. The instance is equipped with 512.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of 3800 GB of high-speed NVMe SSD instance store volumes. Networking capabilities include a 30 Gbps baseline bandwidth managed via the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core processing and memory subsystem performance. The r7gd.16xlarge achieves top-tier status in Geekbench multi-core and PassMark memory tests, placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only and write-only large block transfers scoring in the top 25%. Database operations and Redis SET benchmarks also demonstrate strong performance, executing 101.36 million operations per second. However, single-core capabilities, such as stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core, perform in the average tier. LLM inference benchmarks show a mixed profile, with strong text generation speeds for medium 7B models but poor performance on smaller 135M models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 architecture combined with dense memory allocation and integrated NVMe storage offers a highly resource-dense profile. This eliminates the need for external block storage attachments for high-throughput local data operations. This hardware configuration is highly suited for memory-intensive workloads, large-scale database deployments, Redis caching layers, static web serving, and multi-threaded data processing tasks that benefit from dedicated physical cores and high local storage IOPS.

It features 512.0 GB of RAM, providing 8.0 GB per core, and includes 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance delivers a 30 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark data highlights top-tier performance in Geekbench multi-core and PassMark memory tests, alongside strong results in database operations, Redis SET performance, and large-block memory bandwidth. Conversely, single-core performance and small-model LLM text generation are average to poor. This resource-dense profile offers high qualitative cost efficiency for data-intensive applications by bundling massive memory with fast local storage. It is highly suited for large databases, caching layers, static web serving, and multi-threaded enterprise workloads.
